themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints in East Harlem spiked to 22 this week, a 184% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 7.8 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.14), suggesting a new or worsening traffic pattern affecting residential quality of life.
evidence: 22 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with community board's recurring request to hire additional traffic enforcement agents
reporting_angles: What specific vehicles or routes are driving the spike? Street racing, delivery trucks, or commercial traffic changes?
Interview residents on which blocks are most affected and what times of day impact is worst

themes_detail.label: Lost Property Complaints Jump
themes_detail.summary: Lost property complaints jumped to 5 this week, a 567% spike from the 8-week average of 0.8 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.13), potentially signaling uptick in theft, unattended items, or reporting behavior changes in public spaces.
evidence: 5 lost property complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
May indicate either theft prevalence increase or awareness of reporting mechanism
reporting_angles: Are these complaints clustered in specific subway stations, parks, or commercial areas?
Interview NYPD and community members about whether theft has visibly increased or if residents are newly reporting items they previously would have ignored

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints rose to 79 last week, a 201% increase over the 8-week baseline of 26.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 3.48), representing sustained elevation in outdoor noise disruption.
evidence: 79 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 26.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Part of broader noise pattern in district (residential noise also elevated at 2,093 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Are construction sites, street fairs, or outdoor markets driving the spike?
Which neighborhoods within East Harlem are most affected? Map complaints geographically by block

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment-related 311 complaints spiked to 17 two weeks ago, a 807% increase from the 8-week baseline of 1.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 7.7), indicating visible homelessness concentration or reporting acceleration in the district.
evidence: 17 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Converges with concurrent ERT complaints spike (5 vs. 0.8 avg, +567%) suggesting city response activity
reporting_angles: Which parks, subway stations, or street corners have visible encampments? Map the geographic concentration
Interview outreach teams, shelter operators, and affected residents about causes: new arrivals, shelter capacity issues, or policy changes?

themes_detail.label: Infrastructure Service Requests Surge
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests exploded to 3 two weeks ago (2,300% increase from 0.1 weekly baseline, z-score: 8.69) and root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints hit 4 three weeks ago (540% spike from 0.6 avg, z-score: 3.94), suggesting deteriorating public realm maintenance or heightened community reporting.
evidence: Litter basket requests: 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% increase, z-score: 8.69, highest severity spike)
Root/sewer/sidewalk condition: 4 three weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score: 3.94)
Aligns with community board's recurring request to increase graffiti removal/cleaning budget
reporting_angles: Is this a response to specific street conditions (flooding, potholes, debris accumulation) or inadequate trash infrastructure?
Compare complaint locations—are they clustered near parks, transit hubs, or commercial corridors where baskets are missing?
